pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (danazol), multicenter, superiority trial; 2:1 randomization (MMB:DAN); 24-week randomized treatment period followed by open-label period
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: MFSAF v4.0 TSS response rate (≥50% reduction from baseline) at Week 24; Key secondary: transfusion independence rate at Week 24, spleen volume reduction
pivotal_trials.result: TSS response rate 24.6% (MMB) vs 9.2% (DAN), treatment difference 15.7% (95% CI: 5.5%, 25.8%), p=0.0095; TI rate 30% vs 20% (NI met); SRR ≥25% reduction 39.2% vs 6.2%, p<0.0001; rate of no transfusion by Week 24: 35.4% vs 16.9%, p=0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (ruxolitinib), multicenter, non-inferiority trial; 1:1 randomization; 24-week double-blind treatment period followed by open-label MMB
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: splenic response rate (≥35% spleen volume reduction) at Week 24; Key secondary: TSS response rate (≥50% reduction) at Week 24; transfusion independence rate at Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: SRR 26.5% (MMB) vs 29.5% (RUX); NI treatment difference 9% (95% CI: 2%, 16%), p=0.014 (NI met); TSS NI not demonstrated (28.4% vs 42.2%, p=0.98); TI rate 66.5% vs 49.3%, nominal p<0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (best available therapy), multicenter, superiority trial; 2:1 randomization (MMB:BAT); 24-week randomized treatment period
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: splenic response rate (≥35% spleen volume reduction) at Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: SRR 6.7% (MMB) vs 5.8% (BAT), treatment difference 1% (95% CI: -9%, 10%), p=0.90; trial failed primary endpoint; deemed uninterpretable due to design flaws (89% of BAT arm received ruxolitinib; no washout allowed)

key_safety: The most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were thrombocytopenia (28%), diarrhea (22%), hemorrhage (22%), and fatigue (21%); serious risks include infections (35% of MMB-treated patients), thrombocytopenia (grade 3/4 in ~22% by lab data), neutropenia (ANC <0.5×10⁹/L in 2%), and hepatotoxicity including two probable DILI cases and one hepatitis B reactivation identified across 993 MMB-treated patients in the development program.
target_moa: Inhibitor of JAK1 and JAK2 (including JAK2V617F mutant) and ACVR1/ALK2; JAK1/2 inhibition reduces aberrant cytokine signaling and myeloproliferation; ACVR1 inhibition suppresses hepcidin expression, increasing iron availability and red blood cell production

_meta.indication: OJJAARA is indicated for the treatment of intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis (MF), including primary MF or secondary MF [post-polycythemia vera (PV) and post-essential thrombocythemia (ET)], in adults with anemia.

indication_details.population_restrictions: adults with anemia; intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis (primary MF, post-PV MF, or post-ET MF)
